note: The negative focus reading is assigned only when an exact reviewed negative predicate independently supports it; baan/ayaan are not globally treated as negative because the spellings can overlap subject-clitic combinations.

Under negation plus focus, reduced subjunctive simple and progressive forms do not distinguish present from past or person/number. Exact reviewed Qaamuus negative surfaces are reused contextually; their original tagto/tagto_socota labels identify the independently reviewed spelling source, not a past-only interpretation under focus.
Once a reviewed negative predicate disambiguates baan/ayaan as subject focus, a reviewed common-noun subject must use its absolute focus form rather than the ordinary -u nominative subject surface.

Do not infer habitual or future negative focus from the simple/progressive bridge. Full present ma-forms such as cuno/cunayo are also not substitutes for the reduced baan/ayaan focus-negative construction.
